To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
functional MRI and PET can be used to predict response to (chemo) radiotherapy in head and neck cancer.

the early tumoral changes from radiotherapy can be captured with functional MRI and 2-deoxy-2-[18F] fluoro-D-glucose positron emission tomography (18F-FDG PET) and could allow for personalization of treatment adaptation.
early functional imaging during (radio)chemotherapy can be used to predict treatment response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of functional imaging to detect early intratreatment changes that may be associated with response and survival in head and neck cancer patients.
the development of a method that can be used to predict the outcome of (chemoradiation) therapy in patients with head and neck squamocellular carcinoma (HNSCC).
the development of a new method for predicting LRC and overall survival (LRC) in the presence of a single patient.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current evidence is insufficient to recommend the use of functional imaging to predict response in HNSCC patients.
early functional imaging (CTp, MRI or PET) can be used as a predictive tool in HNSCC patients treated with curative intent, however, more studies with larger patient populations are needed.
the predictive value of functional imaging for LRC or OS is not yet established.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
early functional imaging during (chemo)radiotherapy can predict LRC and OS in patients with head and neck cancer.
functional imaging during radiotherapy can predict locoreginal control and overall survival.
the early functional imaging response to radiotherapy could potentially be used to predict treatment outcome and could be used to personalize treatment adaptation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
functional imaging is a feasible and promising method to monitor treatment response during (chemo)-radiotherapy and could be implemented in clinical practice.
functional MRI and PET can provide prognostic information on LRC and OS during treatment.
the use of functional imaging during chemo-radiotherapy for response prediction is promising.
